00b69189-1ae1-5625-adfb-e5460845c776.title: Finding the Matrix Left Multiplication Equivalent To a Sequence of Row Operations

09d8ec89-4d75-51ac-a870-1d2f8a1800ba.title: Finding the Matrix Left Multiplication Equivalent To a Given Row Operation

before.name: Question 1
before.problem:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ in the given order:

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2},\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}
$$

What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

Question 1
?

Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a 3×3 matrix A in the given order: R1:=R1−2R2,R3:=R3−3R1 What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
[1−20010001]⋅[100010−301]⋅A
b
[100010301]⋅[120010001]⋅A
c
[10−20103−61]⋅[100010−201]⋅A
d
[1200−10301]⋅[1200−10001]⋅A
e
[100010−301]⋅[1−20010001]⋅A
Submit

decision.explanation: Row operations act by left multiplication. The first operation uses the elementary matrix with −2 in position (1,2); the second uses the matrix with −3 in position (3,1). Thus the second matrix multiplies on the left of the first, giving option e.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ in the given order:

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2},\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}
$$

What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
after.worked_solution:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

- The first operation is ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

- The second operation is ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{1}$ on the left and get ${E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to ${E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{2}$ on the left and get ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A

Question 1
?

Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a 3×3 matrix A in the given order: R1:=R1−2R2,R3:=R3−3R1 What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
[1−20010001]⋅[100010−301]⋅A
b
[100010301]⋅[120010001]⋅A
c
[10−20103−61]⋅[100010−201]⋅A
d
[1200−10301]⋅[1200−10001]⋅A
e
[100010−301]⋅[1−20010001]⋅A
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

  • The first operation is R1:=R1−2R2. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R1:=R1−2R2∼[1−20010001]=E1

  • The second operation is R3:=R3−3R1. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R3:=R3−3R1∼[100010−301]=E2

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix A, we multiply by E1 on the left and get E1A:

[1−20010001]⋅A

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to E1A, we multiply by E2 on the left and get E2E1A:

[100010−301]⋅[1−20010001]⋅A

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix Left Multiplication Equivalent To a Sequence of Row Operations
content.problem:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ in the given order:

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2},\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}
$$

What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
content.worked_solution:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

- The first operation is ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

- The second operation is ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{1}$ on the left and get ${E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to ${E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{2}$ on the left and get ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

- The second operation is ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{1}$ on the left and get ${E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to ${E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{2}$ on the left and get ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

before.html:
Question 2
?

Suppose that the elementary row operation R3:=−32R3 is applied to a 3×3 matrix A. What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
[1000100−321]⋅A
b
A⋅[100010−3201]
c
[1000100032]⋅A
d
[10001000−32]⋅A
e
A⋅[10001000−32]
Submit

decision.explanation: Left multiplication by diag(1,1,−3/2) preserves the first two rows of A and multiplies its third row by −3/2. Therefore option d implements the stated row operation.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Suppose that the elementary row operation ${R}_{3}:=-\frac{3}{2}{R}_{3}$ is applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
after.worked_solution:
We need to find a matrix $E$ such that $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{2}:=-\frac{3}{2}{R}_{3}$ to $A.$

To find $E,$ we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{3}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is $EA:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

after.html:
Question 2
?

Suppose that the elementary row operation R3:=−32R3 is applied to a 3×3 matrix A. What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
[1000100−321]⋅A
b
A⋅[100010−3201]
c
[1000100032]⋅A
d
[10001000−32]⋅A
e
A⋅[10001000−32]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We need to find a matrix E such that EA is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation R2:=−32R3 to A.

To find E, we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

I=[100010001]R3:=−32R3∼[10001000−32]=E

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is EA:

[10001000−32]⋅A

verification.explanation: Option d is confirmed by the worked solution: left multiplication by diag(1,1,−3/2) scales only row 3 by −3/2. The solution's initial reference to R2 is a typo; its calculation and final matrix correctly implement the stated R3 operation. Option a instead subtracts 3/2 times row 2 from row 3.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix Left Multiplication Equivalent To a Given Row Operation
content.problem: Suppose that the elementary row operation ${R}_{3}:=-\frac{3}{2}{R}_{3}$ is applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
content.worked_solution:
We need to find a matrix $E$ such that $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{2}:=-\frac{3}{2}{R}_{3}$ to $A.$

To find $E,$ we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{3}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is $EA:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

before.html:
Question 3
?

Suppose that the elementary row operation R1:=R1+4R3 is applied to a 3×3 matrix A. What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
[100010401]⋅A
b
[104010001]⋅A
c
[100010004]⋅A
d
A⋅[100010401]
e
A⋅[104010001]
Submit

decision.explanation: Left multiplication by the identity matrix with 4 in position (1,3) replaces row 1 by R1 + 4R3 and preserves rows 2 and 3. This is option b.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Suppose that the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+4{R}_{3}$ is applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
after.worked_solution:
We need to find a matrix $E$ such that $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+4{R}_{3}$ to $A.$

To find $E,$ we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+4{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is $EA:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Question 3
?

Suppose that the elementary row operation R1:=R1+4R3 is applied to a 3×3 matrix A. What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
[100010401]⋅A
b
[104010001]⋅A
c
[100010004]⋅A
d
A⋅[100010401]
e
A⋅[104010001]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to find a matrix E such that EA is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation R1:=R1+4R3 to A.

To find E, we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

I=[100010001]R1:=R1+4R3∼[104010001]=E

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is EA: [104010001]⋅A

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix Left Multiplication Equivalent To a Given Row Operation
content.problem: Suppose that the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+4{R}_{3}$ is applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
content.worked_solution:
We need to find a matrix $E$ such that $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+4{R}_{3}$ to $A.$

To find $E,$ we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+4{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is $EA:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Question 4
?

Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a 3×3 matrix A in the given order: R3:=−9R3,R1:=R1+3R2,R2:=R2−5R1 What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
[100510001]⋅[1−30010001]⋅[100010009]⋅A
b
[130010001]⋅[100−510001]⋅[10001000−9]⋅A
c
[10001000−9]⋅[130010001]⋅[100−510001]⋅A
d
[100−510001]⋅[130010001]⋅[10001000−9]⋅A
e
[10−5010001]⋅[103010001]⋅[−900010001]⋅A
Submit

decision.explanation: Each row operation multiplies on the left, so the matrices appear in reverse order: first scale row 3 by −9, then add 3 times row 2 to row 1, then subtract 5 times the updated row 1 from row 2. This gives option d.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ in the given order:

$$
{R}_{3}:=-9{R}_{3},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2},\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1}
$$

What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
after.worked_solution:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

- The first operation is ${R}_{3}:=-9{R}_{3}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=-9{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

- The second operation is ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

- The third operation is ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{1}$ on the left and get ${E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to ${E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{2}$ on the left and get ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Finally, to apply the third elementary row operation to ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{3}$ on the left and get ${E}_{3}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$ 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Question 4
?

Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a 3×3 matrix A in the given order: R3:=−9R3,R1:=R1+3R2,R2:=R2−5R1 What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
[100510001]⋅[1−30010001]⋅[100010009]⋅A
b
[130010001]⋅[100−510001]⋅[10001000−9]⋅A
c
[10001000−9]⋅[130010001]⋅[100−510001]⋅A
d
[100−510001]⋅[130010001]⋅[10001000−9]⋅A
e
[10−5010001]⋅[103010001]⋅[−900010001]⋅A
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

  • The first operation is R3:=−9R3. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R3:=−9R3∼[10001000−9]=E1

  • The second operation is R1:=R1+3R2. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R1:=R1+3R2∼[130010001]=E2

  • The third operation is R2:=R2−5R1. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R2:=R2−5R1∼[100−510001]=E3

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix A, we multiply by E1 on the left and get E1A:

[10001000−9]⋅A

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to E1A, we multiply by E2 on the left and get E2E1A:

[130010001]⋅[10001000−9]⋅A

Finally, to apply the third elementary row operation to E2E1A, we multiply by E3 on the left and get E3E2E1A:

[100−510001]⋅[130010001]⋅[10001000−9]⋅A

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option d: successive left multiplications give E3E2E1A. Its resulting rows are R1+3R2, −5R1−14R2, and −9R3, as required. Option c reverses the two row-addition operations and produces different rows.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix Left Multiplication Equivalent To a Sequence of Row Operations
content.problem:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ in the given order:

$$
{R}_{3}:=-9{R}_{3},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2},\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1}
$$

What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
content.worked_solution:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

- The first operation is ${R}_{3}:=-9{R}_{3}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=-9{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

- The second operation is ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

- The third operation is ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{1}$ on the left and get ${E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to ${E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{2}$ on the left and get ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Finally, to apply the third elementary row operation to ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{3}$ on the left and get ${E}_{3}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$ 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -9\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

before.html:
Question 5
?

Suppose that the elementary row operation R2:=3R2 is applied to a 3×3 matrix A. What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
[100013001]⋅A
b
[100310001]⋅A
c
[100010031]⋅A
d
[130010001]⋅A
e
[100030001]⋅A
Submit

decision.explanation: Left multiplication by diag(1,3,1) multiplies row 2 by 3 and preserves rows 1 and 3. Therefore option e implements the stated operation.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Suppose that the elementary row operation 
${R}_{2}:=3{R}_{2}$ is applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
after.worked_solution:
We need to find a matrix $E$ such that $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{2}:=3{R}_{2}$ to $A.$

To find $E,$ we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is $EA:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Question 5

Suppose that the elementary row operation R2:=3R2 is applied to a 3×3 matrix A. What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
[100013001]⋅A
b
[100310001]⋅A
c
[100010031]⋅A
d
[130010001]⋅A
e
[100030001]⋅A
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to find a matrix E such that EA is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation R2:=3R2 to A.

To find E, we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

I=[100010001]R2:=3R2∼[100030001]=E

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is EA:

[100030001]⋅A

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix Left Multiplication Equivalent To a Given Row Operation
content.problem:
Suppose that the elementary row operation 
${R}_{2}:=3{R}_{2}$ is applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A.$ What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
content.worked_solution:
We need to find a matrix $E$ such that $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{2}:=3{R}_{2}$ to $A.$

To find $E,$ we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is $EA:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$
